title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 5 findings on PR #524 head d3d8781
description:
Supervisor self-review round 5 of PR #524 head d3d8781. SIX findings (4 medium, 2 low). No highs; the sweep independently re-verified as clean the interval-overlap algebra, __future__ anchor ordering, revoked/superseded predicates in activeRows, savepoint placement (failed turns leave no ordinal hole), nested withTransaction, the seenRuleIdentities/includeAllActive interaction, and the sessionDebug section labels.

Findings 2, 3 and 4 are all consequences of round 4's __future__ canonicalization. Fix the CLASS: that canonicalization rewrites a value the caller supplied, and every path that reads, returns, or compares that value must agree about which form it is looking at.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev8 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev8, cut from eshyra-jhpt at d3d8781. npm ci already run there.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (medium) — the per-turn degrade path still does not catch the pack-defect class it exists for.
=============================================================
contextAssembler.ts catches CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError and CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError, but assembleCampaignRulesContext -> ambiguitiesFromStack also calls optRulesAmbiguities, which throws RulesPackError on any malformed mechanics.ambiguities block. resolveRulesStack performs only meta-level assertions, so a pack supplied through deps.resolveRulesPack is never record-validated. A record declaring ambiguity id 'ambiguity:Foo_Bar' (fails the kebab-case regex) makes every runTurn throw out of assembleContext and roll back, instead of degrading to ambiguitySourceUnavailable.
This is the THIRD instance of this class: each round a new error type reaches the per-turn path and the catch list does not include it.
FIX: stop enumerating error types. Decide the rule positively — any failure to interpret PACK CONTENT while assembling per-turn context degrades to ambiguitySourceUnavailable with the error recorded; failures that are not about pack content still propagate. Implement it so a future pack-content error class is covered by construction rather than by remembering to add it. State how you achieved that.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (medium) — createCampaignRule returns a rule that does not match what it stored.
=============================================================
writeRule canonicalizes a future-dated prospective effectivePosition to the reserved __future__ anchor, but createCampaignRule returns the CALLER'S rule object, not what was persisted.
REPRODUCED at d3d8781 (supervisor), current ordinal 3, scheduling for ordinal 9:
    returned effectivePosition: {"sessionId":"s1","turnId":"t9","ordinal":9}
    stored   effectivePosition: {"sessionId":"__future__","turnId":"__future__","ordinal":9}
A caller that round-trips the returned value gets different ordering under compareCampaignPositions (future anchors sort before real anchors at equal ordinal) and a position assertPersistedPosition will reject. The existing test asserts canonicalization only via getCampaignRule, so the divergence is uncovered.
FIX: return what was persisted. Test that the returned value deep-equals getCampaignRule for both the future-dated and the ordinary case.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (medium) — same divergence in supersedeCampaignRule.
=============================================================
It returns input.successor rather than what writeRule persisted, so a successor scheduled for a future ordinal is reported with anchors that were rewritten before insert. Same fix, same test shape.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 (medium) — a future-scheduled rule can NEVER be revoked before it takes effect.
=============================================================
Three guards compose into an unsatisfiable constraint: assertCurrentPosition forces currentPosition to equal the latest persisted turn; assertPersistedPosition forces revokedPosition to be a persisted turn; and revokedPosition >= currentPosition. Together those pin revokedPosition to the current ordinal — and the effective-position guard then rejects it for any rule effective later.
REPRODUCED at d3d8781 (supervisor): a rule scheduled at ordinal 9, player changes their mind at ordinal 2 ->
    campaign rule 'sched' cannot be revoked before its effective position
Every revoke attempt fails until ordinal 9 arrives, at which point revoking leaves the rule active for zero turns. There is no way to cancel a scheduled rule. supersedeCampaignRule has no equivalent block, so the two mutations disagree about the same lifecycle.
FIX: cancelling a not-yet-effective rule is a legitimate operation and must be possible. Decide the semantics deliberately — most likely revoking a rule that has not taken effect removes it from ever being active (revocation at its own effective position, or an explicit cancel), rather than requiring a revocation position that cannot exist. Make revoke and supersede consistent about not-yet-effective rules, and say in your notes what you chose. Test: schedule at ordinal 9, cancel at ordinal 2, prove the rule is never active at any position including 9 and later.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 (low) — duplicate governingRecordKeys duplicate the rule in the context packet.
=============================================================
The seam's governed loop pushes one entry per governingRecordKeys element with no dedup, and withRule appends to campaignRules/campaignRulings unconditionally (only routes is dedup-guarded by trigger). validateCampaignRule never rejects duplicate or empty governingRecordKeys, and keysColumn.decode returns the array verbatim. A rule persisted with ['spell:fireball','spell:fireball'] attaches twice, emits two identical placedRules trace entries, and duplicates the prose against the packet byte budget.
FIX: reject duplicate and empty governingRecordKeys in validateCampaignRule (write-side), and make the seam's placement idempotent per (ruleIdentity, governingRecordKey) so restored or legacy rows cannot duplicate either. Test both sides.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 (low) — a house-rule carrying ambiguity provenance is silently dropped from every context branch.
=============================================================
Such a rule is excluded from `rules` (provenance.kind !== 'ambiguity'), from unboundRulings (ruleKind === 'ruling'), and from `rulings` (isAmbiguityRuling requires ruleKind === 'ruling'). validateCampaignRule rejects the pairing on the write path, but migration 0025's CHECK constraints do not, and CheckpointStore restore inserts snapshot rows directly with no domain validation. Restoring such a checkpoint yields a rule active in listCampaignRules that never reaches the DM prompt, with no loss or diagnostic.
This is the silent-disappearance class again, and the same restore-bypass route as round 3 finding 7.
FIX: the context must not silently drop an active rule for any reason. Give the assembly a total accounting — every active rule lands in exactly one branch or is explicitly recorded as unrepresentable, with its identity visible. Consider also whether migration 0025 should carry the CHECK constraint that matches the domain invariant; if you think it should, file a bead rather than editing the merged migration.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against d3d8781; report observed counts and quote the asserted guard messages.
  - Every negative assertion must assert the distinctive guard message.
  - Do not weaken existing tests, do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, eshyra-umyb, or eshyra-jhpt.2.5.
  - Keep every earlier fix intact, especially the deterministic future-anchor ordering from round 4.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-03: codex gpt-5.6-luna, effort HIGH, YOLO, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev8 (cut from eshyra-jhpt @ d3d8781).

Completed on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev8 at the assigned worktree.

Implemented all six round-5 fixes:
1. Pack-content failures carry a shared internal marker and the per-turn assembler catches that positive category, covering RulesPackError and future interpreter failures by construction; the ambiguity interpreter boundary wraps unmarked failures, while unrelated resolver/database failures still propagate.
2. createCampaignRule returns the canonical rule returned by writeRule, and supersedeCampaignRule canonicalizes before comparison and returns the stored successor.
3. A future rule can be explicitly cancelled at the current persisted position; non-current pre-effective revocation remains rejected. Supersession uses the same canonical future representation.
4. governingRecordKeys must be non-empty, non-blank, and unique; discovery placement and placedRules trace are idempotent per rule identity/governing key, including restored legacy rows.
5. Added total context accounting for restored active rows whose provenance cannot be represented, with the identity visible in the rendered campaign-rules section.
6. Added regressions for all of the above, plus a non-pack resolver failure propagation guard.

Negative proof against clean d3d8781 with the six new regression cases: 6 failed, 113 passed (3 focused files; 119 tests total). Asserted guard messages included:
- "campaign rule 'future-to-cancel' cannot be revoked before its effective position"
- "governingRecordKeys must contain at least one record key"
- "governingRecordKeys[0] must be a non-empty string"
- "governingRecordKeys contains duplicate key 'spell:fireball'"
- "feature:malformed-ambiguity.data.mechanics.ambiguities[0].id must be a stable ambiguity:<kebab-case> ID"
- "UNREPRESENTABLE ACTIVE CAMPAIGN RULE restored-invalid-provenance"

Final npm run verify:worktree passed with worktree-local module resolution: 277 test files passed, 3 skipped; 4888 tests passed, 20 skipped. Biome reported only the existing schema-version info (config 2.5.5 vs CLI 2.5.11).

No merged migrations, eshyra-umyb, eshyra-jhpt.2.5, or sibling/parent beads were modified.
